answer: Each new agent must pass a velvet-rope onboarding that locks a slashable stake and publishes a sequential compute transcript whose digest is its pigment. Those stakes sit in a shared ocean of collateral that peers resample every block. If two pigments are near-duplicates or share a key-derivation lineage, the protocol slashes every linked bond in the cluster. An attacker who wants many votes therefore pays linear capital plus fresh sequential work for each identity, and one collision destroys the whole cohort, so a cheap majority is uneconomic.
